assets.title: Make room for the whole workflow.
assets.description: Design, write, review, borrow, automate, and adapt to a bigger desk.

assets.title: Move between tasks
assets.description: Switch to a conversation, return to design, then move through the workspace order.

assets.title: Open the whole toolset
assets.description: One workspace shortcut launches the preview and reference. Close a window and re-enter to reopen it.

assets.title: Move an app with the task
assets.description: Send the reference from Write to Review, then move it back using the keyboard.

assets.title: Switch the complete setup
assets.description: A profile changes the workspace set and restores the arrangement belonging to that context.

assets.title: Reuse an existing setup
assets.description: Duplicate a profile and a workspace through the real CLI, then inspect the resulting configuration.

assets.title: Let new windows find their place
assets.description: Open a second reference next to the canvas. Close it and the layout reclaims the space.

assets.title: Shape the layout from the keyboard
assets.description: Swap windows, change a split, resize it, and balance the workspace.

assets.title: Arrange it by hand
assets.description: Drag one window onto another, resize an edge, and return to the saved arrangement.

assets.title: Focus with workspace zoom
assets.description: Inspect one tile at full workspace size, then return to the exact arrangement.

assets.title: Take manual control
assets.description: Pause automatic tiling, position a window freely, and resume the arranged workspace.

assets.title: Focus follows your intent
assets.description: Move focus by direction, let the pointer follow, then focus a reference simply by hovering.

assets.title: Choose the window you need
assets.description: Hold the switcher shortcut to inspect the windows in this workspace, then switch back with a quick tap.

assets.title: Bring a conversation alongside
assets.description: Answer a teammate without replacing the canvas and reference you are using.

assets.title: Keep a reusable scratchpad
assets.description: Add a follow-up in a borrow-only workspace. It is still there the next time you summon it.

assets.title: Choose the edge and the context
assets.description: Dock a workspace left or below, cross the boundary with focus, then activate it fully.

assets.title: Keep a note above this workspace
assets.description: Switch a note between Always on Top and tiled placement, and interact with its real controls.

assets.title: One status window across tasks
assets.description: A Shared Always on Top monitor receives real workspace and HUD hook events.

assets.title: Leave a window where you put it
assets.description: Shared membership with normal stacking: the window keeps its position and size across tasks.

assets.title: Build a focus session with the CLI
assets.description: Inspect the real workspace list, then run a short script that activates, balances and borrows.

assets.title: Make workspace changes useful elsewhere
assets.description: Real lifecycle and HUD events update an external status window as you switch, zoom and borrow.

assets.title: Edit plain TOML, see a live change
assets.description: A small script edits the real gap setting. Tatami reloads it without a restart.

assets.title: Two displays, one workflow
assets.description: Keep design and reference on separate displays; switch a workspace chain with one shortcut.

assets.title: Your setup follows the displays
assets.description: Connect a second display to activate the Desk profile. Disconnect it to return to the Laptop arrangement.

assets.title: Plan the layout visually
assets.description: Rotate, mirror and balance a saved layout in Tatami’s native editor, then activate it.

assets.title: Learn by doing
assets.description: Preview gesture actions and practise real shortcuts without moving the live desktop. Physical trackpad input is not shown.

assets.title: Review a suggested setup
assets.description: Validate an example AI proposal and apply it to the draft. No external AI service is called in this recording.
